title: Bioinformatics Resources
author: Ahmed Sameh
description: A friendly field guide to learning bioinformatics, building reproducible analyses, and exploring modern biological research.

tracks.title: Build your foundations
tracks.description: Get comfortable with code, biological data, and the questions good analyses ask.
tracks.intro: Start with the skills your first project needs. You can learn the deeper mathematics alongside your work; completing every course here is not an entry requirement.

topics.title: Python, R, and the command line
topics.description: Choose a language for a concrete task, then learn to read, transform, and visualize a small dataset.
topics.prerequisites: No programming experience required.
concepts: Python: variables, functions, tables, plotting, and small scripts.
R: data frames, factors, tidy data, plotting, and biological analysis packages.
Shell: paths, pipes, redirection, permissions, and inspecting a text file.
topics.outcome: Write a short script that reads a table, checks its columns, and saves a useful summary.
topics.practice: Use one small table in either Python or R. Report missing values, summarize one measurement by group, and plot the result. Explain the biological meaning of each column.
topics.caution: Choose one language for your first project. Language preference depends on the analysis and team; you do not need to learn Python and R simultaneously.

topics.title: Biological data and file formats
topics.description: Understand what a file represents before choosing a tool to process it.
topics.prerequisites: Basic molecular biology and the ability to inspect a text file.
concepts: Sequences and reads: FASTA, FASTQ, quality scores, and reference versions.
Alignments and annotation: SAM/BAM, VCF, BED, and GTF/GFF; learn coordinate conventions explicitly.
Analysis objects: count matrices, sample metadata, AnnData, and MuData.
Structures: PDB and mmCIF, chains, residues, assemblies, and identifiers.
topics.outcome: Explain the inputs, outputs, identifiers, and coordinate system of your chosen analysis.
topics.practice: Make a data dictionary for a tutorial dataset. Record its accession, organism, reference genome or structure, sample units, and file formats.
topics.caution: Gene symbols, stable identifiers, and reference builds are not interchangeable. Preserve the versions and mapping decisions used in your analysis.

topics.title: Statistics and experimental design
topics.description: Connect statistical decisions to the biological question and experimental units.
topics.prerequisites: Basic tables and plots; learn probability concepts as needed.
concepts: Biological versus technical replication, controls, randomization, and confounding.
Distributions, effect sizes, uncertainty, hypothesis tests, and multiple testing.
Linear models, covariates, batch effects, and exploratory data analysis.
For single-cell studies, identify the independent biological samples before testing.
topics.outcome: Describe the comparison, independent samples, covariates, and limitations of a small study.
topics.practice: Sketch two experimental designs: one where treatment is confounded with batch, and one where it is balanced. Explain what can be learned from each.
topics.caution: A small adjusted p-value does not establish a large effect or causality. Interpret effect sizes, design, and uncertainty together.

topics.title: Git, environments, and research habits
topics.description: Make it possible for your future self and a collaborator to repeat your work.
topics.prerequisites: A small script or notebook.
concepts: Git commits, branches, readable READMEs, and reviewable changes.
Separate input data, code, configuration, and generated results.
Record package versions, random seeds, parameters, and dataset accessions.
Use environments first; learn containers when your workflow needs portability.
topics.outcome: Share a small project with clear setup and rerun instructions.
topics.practice: Ask a peer to reproduce one plot using only your README. Record any missing dependency, parameter, or data-download instruction and repair it.
topics.caution: A notebook that ran once is not sufficient documentation. Restart the session and rerun it from the beginning before sharing.

topics.title: Mathematics when you need it
topics.description: Build intuition for the mathematics behind the methods you actually use.
topics.prerequisites: School-level algebra; programming helps with experiments.
concepts: Linear algebra: vectors, matrices, projections, eigenvectors, and PCA.
Probability: conditional probability, likelihood, and uncertainty.
Calculus and optimization: gradients, objectives, and iterative fitting.
topics.outcome: Explain one method's inputs, objective, assumptions, and outputs in plain language.
topics.practice: Apply PCA to a small numeric table, then explain what the axes describe and how scaling changes the result.
topics.caution: These topics are deeper study options. Do not delay an accessible first project until you have completed all of them.

tracks.title: Explore structures. Design proteins.
tracks.description: Learn to inspect molecular structures, interpret predictions, and explore protein and binder design.
tracks.intro: Begin by reading experimental structures and assessing their quality. Prediction, molecular simulation, and design are connected paths with different assumptions and validation needs.

topics.title: Structural biology and structure literacy
topics.description: Read a structure as evidence about a molecule and an experiment.
topics.prerequisites: Protein sequence and molecular biology basics.
concepts: Protein architecture, interactions, thermodynamics, and structure–function relationships.
Experimental method, resolution where applicable, missing residues, and validation reports.
Chains, biological assemblies, sequence mapping, and molecular visualization.
topics.outcome: Inspect a structure and write a short account of what it supports and what remains uncertain.
topics.practice: Complete the protein-structure starter project, then locate a missing region or a validation concern in a second entry.
topics.caution: A deposited coordinate model is an interpretation of evidence. Check the experimental method and validation information before drawing conclusions.

topics.title: Structure prediction and confidence
topics.description: Understand the question a prediction answers and how to assess its reliability.
topics.prerequisites: Structure literacy and sequence alignment basics.
concepts: Sequence-to-structure prediction, templates, alignments, and complexes.
Local confidence, relative-domain confidence, and model-specific quality measures.
Sequence correspondence, experimental comparisons, and sources of uncertainty.
topics.outcome: Explain why a predicted region or interface is more or less trustworthy.
topics.practice: Choose a protein with both experimental and predicted structures. Align the sequences first, inspect confidence, and document which regions are comparable.
topics.caution: Confidence scores are not interchangeable with experimental B-factors. A confident prediction alone does not establish binding, function, or a mechanism.

topics.title: Protein and binder design
topics.description: Follow a design problem from a biological objective to candidates that need experimental testing.
topics.prerequisites: Structure prediction and assessment, protein interactions, and basic scripting.
concepts: Target preparation, biological assembly, accessible sites, and design constraints.
Backbone generation, sequence design, structure prediction, and candidate filtering.
Compare diffusion-based backbone design with optimization-based pipelines such as BindCraft.
Diversity, controls, expression and solubility considerations, and experimental validation.
topics.outcome: Describe a candidate-selection strategy and the evidence needed to test a proposed binder.
topics.practice: Read one published design study and map its stages, selection metrics, controls, and experimental outcomes. Begin with published outputs before scheduling expensive generation runs.
topics.caution: A favorable computational score is a screening signal. Report it separately from measured affinity, specificity, and experimental success.

topics.title: Diffusion models in molecular design
topics.description: Connect denoising and conditional generation to a biological design task.
topics.prerequisites: Basic machine learning; probability and linear algebra help with the deeper material.
concepts: Forward corruption, learned denoising, sampling, and conditioning.
Representation choices, geometric constraints, and symmetry.
Training versus inference, diversity, and evaluation beyond visually plausible structures.
topics.outcome: Explain what is generated, what conditions the generation, and how candidates are evaluated.
topics.practice: Draw the sampling process for a binder-design example and identify where target information and constraints enter. Continue with the AI foundations path for the mathematics.
topics.caution: Learn the model's task and representation explicitly. Different diffusion systems do not share identical inputs, outputs, or validation criteria.

topics.title: Molecular simulation and biophysics
topics.description: Explore molecular motion through models with explicit physical assumptions.
topics.prerequisites: Thermodynamics, structural biology, and command-line basics.
concepts: Force fields, parameterization, solvation, and boundary conditions.
Minimization, equilibration, sampling, replicates, and convergence.
Trajectory analysis and the relationship between observables and a biological question.
topics.outcome: Explain the assumptions and sampling limitations of a simulation study.
topics.practice: Follow an introductory simulation example and record the force field, ensemble, integration settings, and analysis choices.
topics.caution: A stable-looking trajectory alone does not demonstrate convergence or establish a biological mechanism.

tracks.title: Make sense of omics data
tracks.description: Move from sequencing foundations to single-cell, multimodal, perturbation, and immune repertoire analyses.
tracks.intro: Choose a biological question and learn one analysis end to end. Bulk analysis, single-cell analysis, and other omics specialisms share foundations, but each needs its own experimental and statistical context.

topics.title: Sequencing and bulk RNA-seq
topics.description: Connect read processing and quantification to sample-level statistical analysis.
topics.prerequisites: Basic R or a Galaxy introduction; statistics and sample metadata.
concepts: Read QC, alignment or quantification, references, and gene-level counts.
Sample-level QC, design formulas, contrasts, and differential expression.
Effect sizes, multiple testing, gene-set interpretation, and reporting.
topics.outcome: Produce a reproducible comparison with a clear design, QC plots, and an interpreted results table.
topics.practice: Start with the count-based RNA-seq project. Then follow a full FASTQ-to-results tutorial to learn where those counts come from.
topics.caution: A count-based tutorial does not teach raw-read processing by itself. Keep normalization for visualization distinct from the model's input requirements.

topics.title: Single-cell RNA-seq foundations
topics.description: Learn the core workflow before adding integration or complex models.
topics.prerequisites: R or Python, count matrices, and experimental design.
concepts: Cell and sample QC, ambient RNA, doublets, and normalization.
Dimensionality reduction, clustering, marker evidence, and cell annotation.
Donor-aware comparisons, pseudobulk approaches, and differential abundance.
topics.outcome: Explain the evidence for an annotation and the experimental unit for a comparison.
topics.practice: Follow one small tutorial in Scanpy or Seurat. Keep a table recording every filtering decision and inspect how one changed threshold affects the result.
topics.caution: Clusters are analytical groupings, and annotation requires biological evidence. Preserve donor metadata throughout the workflow.

topics.title: Dataset integration and scvi-tools
topics.description: Address technical differences while checking that meaningful biological variation is retained.
topics.prerequisites: A complete single-cell workflow, covariates, and batch-effect concepts.
concepts: Integration across datasets versus integration across molecular modalities.
Reference mapping, batch covariates, latent representations, and scVI/scANVI.
Evaluation of biological conservation alongside technical mixing.
topics.outcome: Justify an integration strategy and describe how you checked its consequences.
topics.practice: Compare an unintegrated baseline with one integration method. Inspect known biological groups and sample composition as well as a low-dimensional plot.
topics.caution: A well-mixed embedding is not sufficient evidence of a good integration. Confounded study designs can make technical and biological effects difficult to separate.

topics.title: CITE-seq and multimodal analysis
topics.description: Relate RNA, protein, and chromatin measurements while respecting how they were collected.
topics.prerequisites: Single-cell foundations and basic integration concepts.
concepts: CITE-seq RNA and antibody-derived tags; protein background and modality-specific QC.
Paired versus unpaired measurements, missing modalities, and MuData.
totalVI for RNA–protein data and MultiVI for RNA–chromatin accessibility data.
topics.outcome: Choose a method whose assumptions match the modalities and pairing in the experiment.
topics.practice: Follow the totalVI CITE-seq tutorial. Compare RNA and protein evidence for selected markers and document cases where they disagree.
topics.caution: Multi-omics is broader than single-cell RNA–protein analysis. Describe each modality and its measurement process before selecting an integration tool.

topics.title: Single-cell perturbation analysis
topics.description: Study how cells respond to genetic, chemical, or environmental interventions.
topics.prerequisites: Single-cell foundations, experimental controls, and sample-level inference.
concepts: Perturb-seq design, guide assignment, controls, and perturbation efficacy.
Differential expression, differential abundance, and heterogeneous responses.
Observed-response analysis versus prediction of unseen responses; held-out evaluation.
topics.outcome: Define an appropriate comparison and explain what a model evaluation does and does not test.
topics.practice: Use a Pertpy tutorial to compare perturbations with controls. Record replicate structure, guide assignment choices, and the intended generalization task.
topics.caution: Random cell-level splits can fail to test the generalization you care about. Design evaluation around held-out donors, conditions, or perturbations as appropriate.

topics.title: TCR, BCR, and immune repertoires
topics.description: Connect immune receptor sequences, clonotypes, and cellular phenotypes.
topics.prerequisites: Basic immunology and single-cell data handling.
concepts: V(D)J sequences, chain pairing, productive receptors, and clonotype definitions.
Clonal expansion, diversity, overlap, and sampling depth.
Linking repertoire information to RNA expression and cell states.
topics.outcome: Explain a clonotype definition and distinguish clonal relationships from evidence of antigen specificity.
topics.practice: Complete a Scirpy tutorial and compare two reasonable clonotype definitions. Report how the interpretation changes.
topics.caution: Receptor similarity or clonal expansion alone does not establish shared antigen specificity. Document sequence and grouping criteria.

topics.title: Other omics and directions to explore
topics.description: Keep the wider field visible while choosing a tractable next specialization.
topics.prerequisites: Biological data literacy and statistics.
concepts: Variant analysis, genome annotation, and reference-dependent interpretation.
Proteomics and metabolomics: experimental platforms, quantification, and data processing.
Spatial omics: tissue context, spatial dependence, and assay-specific analysis.
topics.outcome: Choose a specialization and find an introductory workflow appropriate to its data.
topics.practice: Choose one Galaxy learning pathway and map its raw data, processing stages, biological question, and outputs.
topics.caution: This is an orientation to additional fields, not a complete curriculum for each one. Use the specialist training materials for detailed methods.

tracks.title: Build workflows that travel
tracks.description: Turn a working analysis into a documented, testable workflow with Nextflow or Snakemake.
tracks.intro: Workflow engineering is shared across scientific tracks. Learn one engine first, then use a familiar analysis to understand dependencies, portability, and failure recovery.

topics.title: From scripts to reproducible workflows
topics.description: Learn the common ideas before committing to a particular engine.
topics.prerequisites: Shell basics, a working analysis script, and software environments.
concepts: Tasks, input/output contracts, dependency graphs, and configuration.
Versioned software, containers, sample sheets, resource declarations, and logs.
Small fixtures, expected outputs, restart behavior, and provenance.
topics.outcome: Draw and implement a small analysis as a dependency graph.
topics.practice: Run the workflow-basics project as a plain Python script, then reproduce its expected output with one engine.
topics.caution: A workflow engine cannot repair unclear scientific assumptions or an incorrect analysis step. Validate the underlying computation first.

topics.title: Nextflow and nf-core
topics.description: Run, configure, and develop portable pipelines using dataflow concepts.
topics.prerequisites: Workflow concepts and command-line experience.
concepts: Processes, channels, workflow composition, and modules.
Parameters, profiles, containers, executors, and resume behavior.
Using nf-core pipelines and understanding their documentation and quality conventions.
topics.outcome: Run a small Nextflow workflow, change a parameter, and explain its task dependencies.
topics.practice: Complete the official introductory training, then run main.nf in the workflow-basics project and compare its output with the reference file.
topics.caution: Start with a small local test profile. Check the data, storage, and compute requirements before running a production pipeline.

topics.title: Snakemake
topics.description: Express analysis steps as rules connected through their input and output files.
topics.prerequisites: Workflow concepts and basic Python.
concepts: Rules, targets, wildcards, configuration, and dependency graphs.
Software environments, containers, resource declarations, and execution profiles.
Dry runs, logs, reports, and testing small examples.
topics.outcome: Write a small rule-based workflow and inspect what will run before executing it.
topics.practice: Run a dry run and then the Snakefile in the workflow-basics project. Change the input FASTA and predict which output should be recomputed.
topics.caution: Make all dependencies explicit. Hidden files, undeclared parameters, and changing environments undermine reproducibility.

tracks.title: Use AI thoughtfully in research
tracks.description: Understand biological models, work effectively with LLMs, and build agents whose results you can evaluate.
tracks.intro: AI literacy has several entry points. Practical LLM use can begin early; training biological models and building tool-using agents require deeper foundations. Keep the scientific question and evidence visible at every stage.

topics.title: Machine learning and biological models
topics.description: Learn what a model represents, optimizes, and can reasonably generalize to.
topics.prerequisites: Basic Python, statistics, and introductory linear algebra.
concepts: Training, validation, test sets, leakage, baselines, and distribution shift.
Embeddings and transformers; variational autoencoders and latent variables.
Diffusion and conditional generation, with links to molecular design.
Using a pretrained model versus fine-tuning or training a new one.
topics.outcome: Describe a model's objective, input representation, baseline, and evaluation task.
topics.practice: Read one scvi-tools model guide and one protein-design model description. Compare their inputs, objectives, outputs, and evidence of usefulness.
topics.caution: A benchmark score only speaks to its evaluation setup. Ask how data were split and whether the test resembles the intended scientific application.

topics.title: Working with LLMs for science
topics.description: Use an LLM for bounded tasks with explicit context and inspectable outputs.
topics.prerequisites: A clear task and the ability to assess the result or consult a qualified reviewer.
concepts: Provide the question, source material, constraints, and desired output format.
Ground literature summaries in supplied papers and check claims against the original text.
For code assistance, provide schemas and small examples, inspect changes, and run meaningful checks.
Record the model, date, inputs, important instructions, and human verification.
topics.outcome: Create a useful research aid with a record of its sources and checks.
topics.practice: Give an LLM a paper's methods section and ask for a table of reported parameters with supporting quotations and locations. Mark absent information as not reported, then verify every row yourself.
topics.caution: Fluent output can contain incorrect claims, citations, or code. Use suitable public or authorized data and check the service's data-handling terms before supplying unpublished or sensitive material.

topics.title: Agentic AI and scientific tools
topics.description: Connect a model to tools while keeping execution and evaluation observable.
topics.prerequisites: Programming, APIs, practical LLM use, and a reproducible baseline task.
concepts: Tool calling, structured inputs and outputs, retrieval, state, and execution traces.
Bounded tool permissions, explicit stopping conditions, and human review where needed.
Task-level evaluation, failure cases, tool-result verification, and cost tracking.
topics.outcome: Specify and evaluate a small agent against a simpler scripted baseline.
topics.practice: Build a read-only assistant over a few public tutorials. Require source locations for answers and test it on a fixed set of answerable and unanswerable questions.
topics.caution: Start with a narrow task and inspect the trace. Greater autonomy is not itself evidence of better scientific results.

topics.title: Evaluate and document AI-assisted work
topics.description: Make it clear which results come from evidence, computation, and model suggestions.
topics.prerequisites: Practical LLM experience or an introductory machine-learning project.
concepts: Reference examples, baselines, held-out tasks, and explicit success criteria.
Citation verification, numerical checks, reproducible tool outputs, and failure analysis.
Versioned prompts or instructions, model settings, tool versions, and limitations.
topics.outcome: Write a short evaluation report with successes, failures, and reproducibility details.
topics.practice: Compare an LLM-assisted solution with a manual or scripted baseline on five fixed tasks. Report factual accuracy and completion, not just writing quality.
topics.caution: The model's own confidence is not an independent check. Verify important claims and calculations against external evidence or deterministic computation.

resources.title: The Python Tutorial
resources.prerequisites: Some general programming familiarity; complete beginners can start with a guided lesson.
resources.summary: The official language tutorial. Use it as a reference while writing small scripts rather than reading everything before practicing.

resources.title: R for Data Science, second edition

resources.title: Data Carpentry: genomics lessons

resources.summary: Learn project organization, the command line, sequence processing, and computing through biological examples.

resources.title: Elzero: Mastering Python
resources.summary: An Arabic-language programming entry point retained from the original resource list. Pair the lessons with a small biological data task.

resources.title: Ensembl training
resources.summary: Learn to navigate genome annotation, identifiers, comparative data, and Ensembl tools using worked training materials.

resources.title: NCBI Learn
resources.summary: Find official introductions and training for NCBI databases and tools; choose a tutorial that matches your data source.

resources.title: AnnData documentation
resources.summary: Understand the annotated matrix structure used in many Python single-cell workflows, including observations, variables, and layers.

resources.title: PDB-101: understanding PDB data
resources.summary: A welcoming introduction to structure files, experimental information, assemblies, and interpretation.

resources.title: Statistical Thinking for the 21st Century
resources.prerequisites: Basic arithmetic and willingness to work through examples.
resources.summary: Develop statistical reasoning about data, probability, inference, and models before relying on a test by name.

resources.title: Bioconductor: gene-level RNA-seq workflow
resources.prerequisites: Basic R, sample metadata, and introductory statistics.
resources.summary: Connect RNA-seq processing with exploratory analysis and differential expression through a documented workflow.

resources.title: Single-cell Best Practices
resources.prerequisites: Basic Python or R and single-cell biology.
resources.summary: A question-oriented reference for single-cell analysis across modalities, including preprocessing, statistics, and integration.

resources.title: Software Carpentry: Version Control with Git
resources.summary: Practice tracking changes, working with remote repositories, and collaborating on a small project.

resources.title: Conda: managing environments
resources.summary: Create and document isolated software environments, including environment files that can be shared with collaborators.

resources.title: Quarto: getting started
resources.prerequisites: Basic R or Python for executable examples.
resources.summary: Combine analysis, narrative, and outputs in a reproducible report rather than copying results into an unrelated document.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare: Linear Algebra
resources.prerequisites: Algebra; consult the course's own prerequisite guidance.
resources.summary: A deeper route into matrices, projections, and related concepts that support PCA and machine learning.

resources.title: Dive into Deep Learning
resources.prerequisites: Python, probability, linear algebra, and basic calculus for deeper chapters.
resources.summary: Build conceptual and practical foundations in deep learning; select chapters relevant to the model you are studying.

resources.title: RCSB PDB: learning resources
resources.summary: Find experimental structures and inspect entry-specific methods, sequence information, and validation evidence.

resources.title: UCSF ChimeraX tutorials
resources.cost: Tutorials free; software terms vary by use
resources.summary: Learn molecular visualization through worked examples; check the current software license for your intended use.

resources.title: Biopython Tutorial and Cookbook
resources.summary: Practical biological sequence and structure handling, including parsers used in the protein-structure starter project.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI: AlphaFold practical guide
resources.summary: Learn access routes, interpretation, strengths, limitations, and confidence assessment for predicted structures.

resources.title: Interpreting AlphaFold confidence scores
resources.summary: Understand local confidence and relative-domain uncertainty before using a prediction to support a biological claim.

resources.title: ColabFold
resources.prerequisites: Structure prediction basics and familiarity with notebooks or command-line tools.
resources.summary: An accessible prediction toolkit with examples and execution options. Check current compute availability before planning a run.

resources.title: RFdiffusion
resources.cost: Code available; GPU compute may cost
resources.prerequisites: Protein design, structure assessment, and command-line experience.
resources.summary: Explore diffusion-based protein backbone generation and conditional design through the authors' code and examples.

resources.title: ProteinMPNN
resources.prerequisites: Protein structures, sequence design, and scripting.
resources.summary: Study sequence design conditioned on a protein backbone as a distinct stage in a broader design workflow.

resources.title: OpenMM user guide
resources.summary: Learn simulation setup, execution, and analysis with explicit attention to the physical model and settings.

resources.title: GROMACS documentation
resources.prerequisites: Thermodynamics, molecular structures, and command-line use.
resources.summary: A reference for molecular dynamics methods, file formats, commands, and reproducible simulation configuration.

resources.title: DESeq2 vignette
resources.summary: Understand count-based differential expression, model design, contrasts, diagnostics, and interpretation.

resources.title: Galaxy Training Network
resources.prerequisites: Choose an introductory pathway; many require no programming.
resources.summary: Hands-on biological analysis tutorials across sequencing, proteomics, metabolomics, and other domains.

resources.title: nf-core/rnaseq
resources.cost: Code free; compute and storage may cost
resources.prerequisites: RNA-seq concepts, Nextflow, and suitable compute access.
resources.summary: A production workflow to examine after a smaller tutorial; learn its inputs, profiles, QC outputs, and documented options.

resources.title: Scanpy tutorials
resources.summary: Work through Python single-cell analysis examples and inspect how preprocessing decisions affect downstream results.

resources.title: Seurat guided clustering tutorial
resources.summary: An R entry point to single-cell QC, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and marker exploration.

resources.title: scvi-tools tutorials and model guides
resources.summary: Choose probabilistic models by task and modality, and read their assumptions alongside the worked tutorials.

resources.title: totalVI: RNA and protein analysis
resources.prerequisites: CITE-seq concepts, Python, and single-cell QC.
resources.summary: A model guide for joint RNA–protein analysis, with links to CITE-seq examples and discussion of the observation model.

resources.title: MultiVI: RNA and chromatin accessibility
resources.summary: Study joint RNA–chromatin accessibility modeling, including the paired and unpaired data setting.

resources.title: MuData documentation
resources.summary: Understand how multimodal observations and modality-specific matrices are organized and linked.

resources.title: Pertpy: perturbation analysis
resources.summary: Explore guide assignment, perturbation efficacy, response comparisons, and prediction through documented examples.

resources.title: Scirpy: immune receptor analysis
resources.prerequisites: Python, single-cell data, and basic immunology.
resources.summary: Learn repertoire QC, clonotype analysis, and integration of receptor information with cell-level measurements.

resources.title: AIRR Community documentation
resources.summary: Use community terminology, data standards, and metadata guidance when handling receptor repertoire datasets.

resources.title: EMBL-EBI on-demand training
resources.summary: Find focused introductions to biological databases and analysis areas, including routes into additional omics fields.

resources.title: Nextflow documentation
resources.summary: Reference processes, channels, modules, profiles, executors, and dependency handling while building a small pipeline.

resources.title: Nextflow community training
resources.prerequisites: Basic shell skills; start with the introductory material.
resources.summary: A guided route from running a first pipeline to composing and configuring workflows.

resources.title: nf-core documentation
resources.summary: Learn conventions for using and developing community pipelines, including configuration and contribution guidance.

resources.title: Snakemake documentation
resources.summary: Understand rules, file dependencies, software environments, execution, and reporting.

resources.title: Snakemake general-use tutorial
resources.summary: Build and extend an example workflow while learning dependency handling, configuration, and execution.

resources.title: Apptainer user guide
resources.summary: Learn container execution and reproducibility concepts relevant to shared research computing systems.

resources.title: Google Machine Learning Crash Course
resources.prerequisites: Python and introductory algebra/statistics; check module guidance.
resources.summary: An applied introduction to model fitting, generalization, data handling, and evaluation.

resources.title: Developing Software with Generative AI
resources.prerequisites: Some programming experience; this is an evolving Carpentries Incubator lesson.
resources.summary: Practice AI-assisted software development through a research-computing lesson. The material is under development; check its current status and verify generated code.

resources.title: Hugging Face LLM course
resources.prerequisites: Python and introductory machine learning for implementation chapters.
resources.summary: Understand language models and their practical ecosystem; pair technical learning with source verification and task-level checks.

resources.title: Hugging Face Agents Course
resources.cost: Course free; external services may cost
resources.prerequisites: Python, APIs, and basic LLM familiarity.
resources.summary: An introduction to agent concepts, tools, and implementation. Evaluate any example on a bounded scientific task before expanding it.

resources.title: Ten simple rules for using large language models in science
resources.prerequisites: A scientific task you want to support with an LLM.
resources.summary: A science-specific starting point for transparent, critical LLM use, with discussion of verification and appropriate applications.

resources.title: BindCraft
resources.cost: Code available; dependency licenses and GPU costs vary
resources.prerequisites: Binder design, structure assessment, and suitable GPU access.
resources.summary: An optimization-based binder-design pipeline combining AlphaFold-based design, sequence design, and filtering. Compare its strategy with diffusion-based approaches and inspect dependency terms.

projects.title: Your first RNA-seq comparison
projects.description: Use a small packaged airway count dataset to compare treated and untreated samples while accounting for cell line.
projects.question: Which genes show evidence of a treatment-associated expression change in this paired experimental design?
projects.prerequisites: Basic R, count matrices, and introductory experimental design.
projects.data: The Bioconductor airway example dataset: four cell lines measured with and without dexamethasone. Starts from counts, not FASTQ files.
outputs: Sample metadata and a PCA plot
A differential-expression table with effect sizes and adjusted p-values
An MA plot and software session information
steps: Read the sample metadata and explain why cell line belongs in the design.
Run the supplied R script and inspect the PCA before interpreting differential expression.
Choose three genes, report effect sizes and adjusted p-values, and state the limits of the comparison.
Use the linked full RNA-seq workflow to learn how raw reads become counts.

projects.title: Read your first protein structure
projects.description: Inspect the experimental crambin structure 1CRN and turn its metadata and residue information into a short scientific report.
projects.question: What does this experimental structure show, and what evidence should accompany a structural interpretation?
projects.data: RCSB PDB entry 1CRN, downloaded as mmCIF by the supplied script. The entry is an experimental structure, not an AlphaFold prediction.
outputs: A downloaded mmCIF file and a residue summary table
A report of experimental method, resolution, chains, and residue counts
An interpretation exercise linking structure to validation information
steps: Run the supplied script, open the structure in a molecular viewer, and identify chains and secondary structure.
Read the entry's experimental and validation information before describing its quality.
Explain what the residue B-factors represent in this experimental context.
For a later extension, choose a matched experimental/predicted protein pair and assess sequence correspondence and prediction confidence.

projects.title: One analysis, two workflow engines
projects.description: Calculate sequence GC content with a plain script, then reproduce the same output using Nextflow or Snakemake.
projects.question: How can explicit dependencies make a small analysis easier to run and verify?
projects.prerequisites: Python and shell basics; install one workflow engine for the extension.
